about: Tweets written by hand for TweetLens to trip sentiment models up. Each one has the label a careful human reader would give it and a sentence on why it is hard.

tests.text: Not bad at all, honestly
tests.why: Two negative words, bad and not, that cancel out.

tests.text: I don't hate it
tests.why: A negated negative word. Mildly positive, not negative.

tests.text: Not the worst film I've seen this year
tests.why: Faint praise: worst is negated but nothing good is said.

tests.text: I can't say I enjoyed a single minute of it
tests.why: The negation sits several words before enjoyed.

tests.text: Oh great, my flight is delayed again. Just what I needed.
tests.why: Every positive word is meant ironically.

tests.text: Wow, thanks for losing my luggage. Really appreciate it
tests.why: Thanks and appreciate praise the very thing being complained about.

tests.text: I just love waiting on hold for three hours
tests.why: Love is sincere in form and sarcastic in meaning.

tests.text: Yeah because Mondays are the best
tests.why: The because-clause signals mockery, not praise.

tests.text: Movie ekdum bakwas thi yaar, paisa barbaad
tests.why: Romanised Hindi: totally rubbish, money wasted. No English sentiment words at all.

tests.text: Aaj ka match zabardast tha, maza aa gaya!
tests.why: Today's match was awesome, it was fun. Only the Hinglish words carry the tone.

tests.text: Service bilkul achhi nahi thi
tests.why: Hindi puts nahi (not) after the word it negates: good, not.

tests.text: Thank you bhai, tum bahut achhe ho
tests.why: Mixed English and Hindi; the praise is in Hindi.
No words at all. Tears of joy means laughter.
No words at all; only the emoji carries anger.
A single symbol.
Fire means great here, not danger.

tests.text: The food was great but the service was painfully slow
tests.why: What follows but usually decides the tone.

tests.text: It started boring but the ending blew me away
tests.why: Boring comes first; the verdict comes after but.

tests.text: Nice phone, shame about the battery
tests.why: A compliment followed by the complaint that matters.

tests.text: Expensive, but worth every penny
tests.why: A drawback conceded, then outweighed.

tests.text: This is soooooo goooood!!!
tests.why: Stretched spelling hides the word good from a plain dictionary.

tests.text: WORST. DAY. EVER.
tests.why: Capitals and full stops add force, not words.

tests.text: meh
tests.why: One short word of disappointment.

tests.text: best. thing. ever.
tests.why: Fragmented emphasis without capitals.

tests.text: luv this sooo much, ur the best
tests.why: Love and your are misspelled on purpose.

tests.text: this phone is trash, battery died in 2hrs smh
tests.why: Trash and smh (shaking my head) are slang.

tests.text: that concert was sick, no cap
tests.why: Sick means excellent here.

tests.text: the new update is lowkey mid
tests.why: Mid means mediocre in current slang.

tests.text: Kill the process and restart the server
tests.why: Kill is a technical instruction, not violence.

tests.text: The documentary about the war airs tonight at 9
tests.why: War is the subject, not the writer's feeling.

tests.text: Is the new update any good?
tests.why: Good appears inside a question.

tests.text: Storm warning lifted for the county at 6pm
tests.why: A news update; the charged word warning is being withdrawn.

tests.text: Flying with them tomorrow #NeverAgain
tests.why: The whole verdict is inside the hashtag.

tests.text: Finally got my visa! #blessed
tests.why: A lowercase hashtag that has to be read as a word.

tests.text: Three hours at the DMV #FML
tests.why: An abbreviation inside a hashtag.

tests.text: Morning run done #GoodVibesOnly
tests.why: Three words joined in capitals.
